title: Initial velocity, acceleration and their spatial derivatives vanish off a closed set fixed by the family
statement: Let N ∈ ℕ (ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), let K ⊆ ℝᴺ be closed, and let φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ satisfy φ t x = x for every t ∈ (−1,1) and every x ∉ K. Put X := initialVelocity φ, X(x) = deriv (s ↦ φ s x) 0, and Z := initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = deriv (t ↦ deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t) 0. Then for every x ∉ K: X(x) = 0, Z(x) = 0, fderiv ℝ X x = 0 and fderiv ℝ Z x = 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (K : Set (Rn N)) (φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N), IsClosed K → (∀ t ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x, x ∉ K → φ t x = x) → ∀ x, x ∉ K → initialVelocity φ x = 0 ∧ initialAcceleration φ x = 0 ∧ fderiv ℝ (initialVelocity φ) x = 0 ∧ fderiv ℝ (initialAcceleration φ) x = 0
